newsitem.title: UK: UK IMRO fines Lincoln Unit Trust Managers and LIV.
newsitem.headline: UK IMRO fines Lincoln Unit Trust Managers and LIV.

text.p: British investments watchdog the Investment Management Regulatory Organisation (IMRO) said on Thursday it had fined Lincoln Unit Trust Managers Ltd and LIV Ltd a total of 20,000 pounds ($32,400) for rule breaches.

It said Gloucester-based Lincoln, formerly Lincoln Fund Managers Ltd, and LIV, formerly Lincoln Investment Management Ltd, did not bank PEP (personal equity plan) customers' money on time and did not have adequate compliance monitoring in some areas between April 1993 and February 1995.

Lincoln breached IMRO rules by not paying the money it received from around 700 PEP applications, around 25 percent of the total, into a client money bank account within the required period between January 1 1994 and January 31 1995.

Between April 1993 and February 1995 Lincoln "did not have adequate procedures for monitoring that client money was banked properly nor that orders were executed as soon as reasonably practicable", IMRO said.

And LIV "did not have adequate procedures for monitoring that investments were suitable nor that allocations were made in accordance with uniform standards and procedures, nor that best execution was provided," the watchdog added.

IMRO said that at the time of the breaches LIV was a fund management company with approximately 1.1 billion pounds under management while Lincoln, an authorised trust manager, managed nine trust units and PEPs and had around 479 million pounds under management. Both firms have remedied the deficiences and will pay costs of 30,000 pounds. ($ = 0.616 British Pounds)
